related_questions.snippet: If you have a particularly bad flare-up, you may be prescribed a short course of steroid tablets to reduce the inflammation in your airways. A 5-day course of treatment is usually recommended, as long-term use of steroid tablets can cause troublesome side effects such as: weight gain. mood swings.

related_questions.question: How long does it take to recover from a COPD flare-up?
related_questions.snippet: COPD flare-ups usually last for seven to ten days, but it might take you longer to feel completely back to normal. Most people fully recover within four to six weeks, but some people never feel as well as they did before their COPD flare-up. 1 in 5 people still have symptoms eight weeks after a COPD flare-up.

related_questions.question: Can you have good and bad days with COPD?
related_questions.snippet: The disease is often experienced as a series of ups and downs, with good days and bad days. In everyday life, people with COPD need to adjust their activities to their current level of fitness. It is important to be familiar with your own body, have an understanding of COPD, and know how to deal with symptoms.

text_blocks.snippet: COPD flare-ups, also known as exacerbations, require prompt treatment to manage symptoms and prevent worsening. Treatment typically involves quick-relief inhalers, oral corticosteroids, antibiotics (if a bacterial infection is suspected), and oxygen therapy. Additionally, lifestyle adjustments like staying active, maintaining a healthy diet, and learning pursed-lip breathing are crucial for long-term management.
snippet_highlighted_words: quick-relief inhalers, oral corticosteroids, antibiotics (if a bacterial infection is suspected), and oxygen therapy

list.title: Quick-Relief Inhalers:
list.snippet: These are often the first line of defense, providing rapid relief from shortness of breath and wheezing. Bronchodilators like albuterol are commonly used.

list.title: Oral Corticosteroids:
list.snippet: These medications, such as prednisone, help reduce inflammation in the airways, making it easier to breathe.

list.title: Antibiotics:
list.snippet: If a bacterial infection is suspected to be the cause of the flare-up, antibiotics may be prescribed to combat the infection.

list.title: Oxygen Therapy:
list.snippet: Supplemental oxygen can improve blood oxygen levels and ease shortness of breath during a flare-up.

list.title: Nebulizers:
list.snippet: If inhalers are not sufficient, a nebulizer can deliver medication in a mist form for easier breathing.

list.title: Pulmonary Rehabilitation:
list.snippet: This program includes exercise training, education, dietary advice, and psychological support to help manage COPD and improve overall well-being.

list.title: Pursed-Lip Breathing:
list.snippet: This technique helps slow breathing, improve oxygen levels, and reduce breathlessness.

list.title: Lifestyle Adjustments:
list.snippet: Staying active, maintaining a healthy diet, and managing stress can help prevent and manage COPD flare-ups.

text_blocks.snippet: When to Seek Further Medical Attention:
If symptoms do not improve within 48 hours of starting treatment, or if symptoms worsen, it's crucial to contact a healthcare provider or go to the hospital, according to UF Health.
